title: Weekend Plans
tagline: Say what you do, where, when and how often, and invite someone along.
hook: Leo and Hana are comparing weekends and Noa wants in. You'll need verbs, a handful of particles and the magic of ませんか.
goals: Build a polite sentence with ます verbs
Pick the right particle: を, で, に, へ
Invite with ませんか and talk about frequency

points.title: 〜ます / 〜ません
points.formula: verb (ます-stem) + ます / ません
explain: The polite verb ending ます covers both "do" and "will do". The negative is ません. Look at the ending, not at a separate tense word.
Verbs sit at the very end of the sentence, after everything else. Subject, time, place, object, then the verb.

examples.ja: わたしは|コーヒーを|飲みます。
あした|学校へ|行きません。
examples.en: I won't go to school tomorrow.

examples.ja: 毎日|日本語を|勉強します。

points.tip: A verb in ます form is complete on its own: 食べます is a whole polite sentence.
points.watch: ます verbs always end the sentence. ませんか joins them to a question.

points.title: を · で · に · へ
points.formula: object を / place で / time or goal に / direction へ
points.gist: Four particles that point at the parts of an action.
explain: を marks what the verb acts on (the object). で marks where an action happens. に marks a point in time or a destination. へ points a direction and is read "e".
Think of each particle as a label stuck onto a noun so the listener knows its job in the sentence.

examples.ja: 図書館で|本を|読みます。
examples.en: I read a book at the library.

examples.ja: 七時に|学校へ|行きます。
examples.en: I go to school at seven.

points.tip: Ask two questions: what is acted on (を) and where does it happen (で)?
points.watch: Use に, not で, with 行く, 来る and 帰る when you name the destination (either に or へ works).

points.title: 時間 + に
explain: When you name a specific time (七時, 土曜日), add に. Words like 毎日, あした and きょう don't take に.
Times come near the start of the sentence, before the place and the object.

examples.ja: 土曜日に|海へ|行きます。
examples.en: I go to the sea on Saturday.

examples.ja: 八時に|ごはんを|食べます。
あした|友だちに|会います。

points.tip: Days of the week and clock times take に. Relative words (あした, きのう) don't.
points.watch: あしたに is wrong; あした stands alone.

points.title: 〜ませんか
explain: Turn the negative into a question and you get an invitation: 行きませんか sounds like "wouldn't you like to go?". It's softer than asking directly.
The reply "yes, let's" is ええ、いいですね or はい、行きましょう.

examples.ja: いっしょに|映画を|見ませんか。
examples.en: Would you like to watch a movie with me?

examples.ja: 土曜日に|海へ|行きませんか。
examples.gloss: on Saturday|to the sea|won't you go?
examples.en: Would you like to go to the sea on Saturday?

points.tip: Put いっしょに in front to make the invitation clear.
points.watch: ませんか is an invitation, not "don't you...?" in the negative sense.

points.title: よく · ときどき · あまり · ぜんぜん
explain: Frequency words go right before the verb. よく is often, ときどき is sometimes.
あまり (not very often) and ぜんぜん (not at all) must be paired with a negative verb: あまり 行きません.

examples.ja: あまり|映画を|見ません。
examples.en: I don't watch movies very often.

examples.ja: ぜんぜん|コーヒーを|飲みません。
examples.en: I don't drink coffee at all.

points.tip: 毎日 (every day) is the biggest, ぜんぜん (never) the smallest.
points.watch: あまり and ぜんぜん without ません sound wrong.

drills.ja: わたしは コーヒーを 飲み＿。
drills.why: The polite present positive ending is ます.

drills.q: Which is the polite negative of 食べます?
drills.why: Swap ます for ません.

drills.ja: 図書館＿ 本を 読みます。
drills.en: I read a book at the library.
drills.why: で marks where the action happens.

drills.en: I go to school at seven.

drills.ja: 土曜日＿ 海へ 行きます。
drills.en: I go to the sea on Saturday.

options: あしたに 行きます。
土曜日に 行きます。
drills.why: あした doesn't take に.

drills.ja: いっしょに 映画を 見＿か。
drills.en: Would you like to watch a movie together?
drills.why: ませんか is a polite invitation.

drills.en: Won't you go to the sea with me?

drills.ja: あまり 映画を 見＿。
drills.en: I don't watch movies very often.
drills.why: あまり needs a negative verb.

options: よく 音楽を 聞きます。
あまり 音楽を 聞きます。
ぜんぜん 音楽を 聞きます。
よく 音楽を 聞きません。
drills.why: よく goes with a positive verb.

drills.prompt: Type the reading of 映画 (movie) in hiragana.
